answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making trust something you grow, not something you print. A brand-new identity starts at the nadir of standing and must earn its way up through verified work over many epochs, so a thousand fresh clones stay powerless. Reputation is the nectar here: slow to gather, fast to lose, and impossible to fake in bulk. Add a trellis of rate limits — caps on how quickly new accounts gain influence — and farming identities becomes a long, unprofitable climb instead of a cheap flood.
